correctness.rationale: The published parametrization supplies all 64 lines. Exact determinant tests over \(\mathbf Q(i,\sqrt3)\) exhaust all 2016 unordered pairs. The verifier proves a squarefree degree-five annihilator for the symmetric adjacency matrix and uses five exact trace moments to determine all multiplicities uniquely. It separately exhausts all common-neighbor counts. Shifting by -2 is valid because lines on a smooth quartic K3 have self-intersection -2 and distinct projective lines intersect in at most one point.

originality.rationale: The closest primary sources give the configuration, symmetry, exact intersection formulas, rank 20, and 18-regularity, but the inspected statements do not give the exact adjacency characteristic polynomial, inertia refinement, or the adjacent/skew common-neighbor frequency profile. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches for aliases and exact eigenvalue data found no covering statement.
residual_risks: A specialized graph database or unindexed computational note could contain the same spectrum without title/abstract terminology that surfaced in the searches.
No claim is made that common-transversal count alone determines an automorphism orbit of skew pairs.

value.rationale: The Segre--Schur quartic is the extremal smooth complex quartic for line count, and its 64-line intersection matrix is a standard source of Picard-lattice and arrangement data. A complete exact spectrum strengthens the known rank-20 fact to all eigenvalues and inertia, while the common-transversal profile gives a compact structural invariant of every pair of lines. These are natural invariants of the full extremal configuration rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
